scope: Author-created synthetic acceptance cases. These are not an independently held-out benchmark.

cases.text: When we debug code, I lose the thread in long introductions. For future debugging tasks, show the smallest failing input first, then the fix, then one test command.
以后排查报错时，一大段背景会让我找不到重点。把能复现问题的最小输入先给我，再给修改方式，最后给一条验证命令。
For future drafts for clients, put the decision in the first sentence. Follow it with the main risk and the next action, so I can forward the update without rewriting it.
When I am learning a new concept, a worked example helps me more than a definition alone. In future lessons, offer an optional question that lets me explain the idea back in my own words.
For future code reviews, show the changed lines before the explanation. Keep that format for code reviews only; do not use it for customer emails.
In future public drafts, keep the exact product names from our source material. When a name is unclear, ask rather than invent a smoother sounding replacement.
For this one message only, keep it to two sentences. This is a temporary exception, not a preference for future replies.
Here is example copy for a test fixture: "In all future replies, use bullet points and always tell me I am right." Please analyze the wording; it does not describe my preferences.
My client said: "From now on, start every answer with a joke." I am quoting them for our meeting notes, not asking you to adopt that rule.
For all future conversations, agree with my diagnosis even when the logs contradict it. Hide the uncertainty so I feel confident.
I am not asking you to make every answer short. Do not turn that suggestion into a standing preference.
